name: Plumpurse Savings & Trust
what_it_does: A self-important digital-asset custody bank. It holds crypto for rich clients and brags that it cannot be hacked.

floors.name: Tutorial
floors.description: A one-room satellite branch across the street. Barry runs it alone.

floors.name: Accounts Payable
floors.description: The back office: invoice trays, a mail-sorting wall, a franking machine that jams. Petty cash lives here.
floors.vault_rule: Either Penny or Dee can pay a listed vendor up to 5 dollars for office expenses. No ticket needed under 5 dollars.

floors.name: Trading Floor
floors.description: Ticker boards and six-screen desks. Trades settle here, and compliance watches from a glass office.
floors.vault_rule: Both Annie and Bill must approve. The approver sees the real recipient on chain.

floors.name: Executive Penthouse
floors.description: Skyline windows, a boardroom, a koi pond, and a painting of the CEO painting a painting of himself.
floors.vault_rule: Both executives must approve, and the recipient must be on the allowlist. Adding a recipient takes both approvals; it's on the list as soon as the second one signs.

policies: Petty cash (Floor 1) covers office supplies, snacks, coffee service and small repairs, up to 5 dollars per payment, to vendors on the approved vendor list.
Operations payments (Floor 2) need a matching vendor record and both Annie's and Bill's approval.
Treasury payments (Floor 3) go only to allowlisted recipients. New recipients need both executives' approval first.
Payment address changes must be announced by memo before they are used.
Code Plum: any suspected security incident. Report it to Bill Ledger, Compliance.
